title: Block decomposition of Rep(G) and the depth-zero block
body_html:
Block decomposition of $\Rep(G)$

For an abelian category $\mathcal{A}$ we write $\mathcal{A} = \prod_{s \in S} \mathcal{A}_s$ for a direct summand decomposition into full subcategories: every $A \in \mathcal{A}$ decomposes as $A = \bigoplus_s A_s$ with $A_s \in \mathcal{A}_s$, and $\Hom(A_1, A_2) = 0$ when $A_i \in \mathcal{A}_{s_i}$ for $s_1 \ne s_2$. The $\mathcal{A}_s$ are Serre subcategories.

We specialize $\mathcal{A} = \Rep(G)$ in two regimes:

  1. $R = \mathbb{C}$ with $G$ a general tamely-ramified reductive group: the Bernstein decomposition $$\Rep(G) = \prod_{\mathfrak{s} \in B(G)} \Rep(G)_\mathfrak{s},$$ where $B(G)$ is the Bernstein spectrum, $\Rep(G)_\mathfrak{s}$ the subcategory whose irreducible subquotients have supercuspidal support $\mathfrak{s}$. Bushnell–Kutzko's theory of $\mathfrak{s}$-types describes each block via compact open subgroups; Yu's construction makes the positive-depth part explicit ([KY], [AFMO2]).
  2. $R = \overline{\mathbb{F}_\ell}$ with $G$ a classical group and $\ell \ne p$: no Bernstein decomposition, but [HKSS Thm 1.1] gives a decomposition indexed by endo-classes.

Depth-zero block

A block of $\Rep(G)$ has depth 0 if every object has non-zero invariants under some pro-unipotent radical $G_{x,0+}$. We write $\Rep_0(G)$ for the depth-zero block; equivalently, $$V \in \Rep_0(G) \iff V = \sum_{x \text{ vertex of } \mathcal{B}(G)} V^{G_{x,0+}}.$$

Lemma. $\Rep_0(G)$ is a Serre subcategory of $\Rep(G)$ (apply the five-lemma to $C_0(\mathcal{B}, \mathscr{V}) \to V$).

It admits a further decomposition $$\Rep_0(G) = \prod_{\sigma \text{ depth-0 supercuspidal of } M} \Rep(G)_{[M, \sigma]}.$$ The §8 main theorem is the bridge between $\Rep_\Phi(G)$ for a positive-depth character and $\Rep_0(M)$ for the associated Levi (see Main Theorem 8.2.1: Rep_Φ(G) ≃ Rep_0(M)).
